steps.title: Seed and grow HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Seed 5 × 10⁵ cells per mL in a 10 cm dish containing 10 mL DMEM with 10 % FBS and 1 % PenStrep; incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Check confluency before transfection
steps.instruction: Verify cells have reached 70‑80 % confluency; if lower, allow additional growth time before proceeding.

steps.title: Prepare transfection mixture
steps.instruction: In a sterile 15 mL Falcon tube, add 3 mL Opti‑MEM, then add plasmid DNA to obtain 15 µg total; pipette 20× and incubate 5 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Add 60 µL Lipofectamine 2000 (4 µL per µg DNA, 4:1 ratio) to the DNA‑Opti‑MEM mixture; pipette 30× and incubate 25 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Transfect cells and incubate
steps.instruction: Add the transfection mixture dropwise to the 10 cm dish while gently agitating; incubate the cells overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Wash cells and collect lysate
steps.instruction: Aspirate media and wash each dish twice with 10 mL 1× PBS (or PBS ++ if cells detach); keep dishes on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL cold lysis buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl, 250 mM sucrose, 250 µM CaCl₂, 1 phosphatase tablet, 1 protease tablet, pH 7.4) containing fresh inhibitors; scrape cells and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube; keep on ice.

steps.title: Mechanical lysis of cells
steps.instruction: Pass the lysate through a sterile 25‑gauge needle 20 times, vortex 30 s, pause, vortex another 30 s, then pass through a 27‑gauge needle 40 times.

steps.title: Low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 700 × g (room temperature) to pellet nuclei and large organelles; keep the supernatant on ice.

steps.title: First ultracentrifugation of membrane fraction
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to ultracentrifuge tubes (≤ 600 µL per tube, balanced); ultracentrifuge at 100 000 × g (40 000 rpm TLA‑55) for 1.5 h at 4 °C (minimum 1 h).

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend membrane pellet
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL fresh lysis buffer with fresh inhibitors to the pellet; pipette a few times and pass through a 25‑gauge needle ≥ 10 times to fragment the pellet.

steps.title: Second ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer 400 µL of the resuspended pellet to a fresh ultracentrifuge tube; ultracentrifuge again at 100 000 × g (40 000 rpm) for 1.5 h at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Remove the supernatant; the pellet (membrane fraction) may be stored at –20 °C for up to 5 days, covered with parafilm and 20‑50 µL lysis buffer.

steps.title: Resuspend in resuspension buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 100–200 µL resuspension buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl, 250 mM NaCl, 90 % glycerol, pH 8.0) by passing through a 27‑gauge syringe ≥ 10 times until no visible clumps remain.

steps.title: Ligand treatment of membrane pellet
steps.instruction: If testing a ligand, add the ligand to the resuspended pellet at the desired concentration (e.g., 128.4 nM EphrinA‑1 Fc) and add an equal volume of the ligand solvent to control samples; mix 20–30× and incubate 1 h on ice protected from light.

steps.title: Add DIBMA polymer
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 µL of 10 % (w/v) DIBMA in PBS per 100 µL lysate (final 0.015 % w/v, acceptable range 0.015–2 % w/v); mix 20–30×.

steps.title: Overnight vortex solubilization
steps.instruction: Parafilm‑seal the 1.5 mL tubes, place them in a vortex adaptor, and vortex at medium speed overnight (12–18 h) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Clarify DIBMALPs by ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer ≥ 100 µL of the overnight mixture to a fresh ultracentrifuge tube; ultracentrifuge at 100 000 × g (40 000 rpm) for 1.5 h at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Remove the supernatant (this is the DIBMALP preparation) and keep it on ice, protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare Trolox solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg Trolox powder in 40 mL deionized water; shake overnight at 4 °C in the dark; filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter; store at 4 °C protected from light (use within 2–3 weeks, discard if colored).

steps.title: Prepare oxygen scavenging system
steps.instruction: On the day of use, combine 1 mL Trolox solution, 40 µL 100 mM PCA (pH 9.0), and 1 µL rPCO (300 U) to make the OSS; keep on ice and protected from light.

steps.title: Make fluorescence calibration standards
steps.instruction: Using a 100 nM GFP stock in 1× PBS, prepare the dilutions listed in Table 1 (0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20 nM) by mixing appropriate volumes of stock with T50 buffer; prepare duplicates or triplicates.

steps.title: Plate calibration standards
steps.instruction: Vortex each standard, then add 100 µL to individual wells of a black opaque 96‑well plate; keep the plate protected from light.

steps.title: Dilute DIBMALPs for assay
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:10 dilution of the DIBMALP sample by adding 10 µL DIBMALP to 90 µL T50 buffer.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence of standards and samples
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of each diluted sample to separate wells (duplicates/triplicates); read fluorescence on a plate reader with excitation 460 nm, emission 495–600 nm, step 1 nm, top optics, normal speed, read height 7.00 mm; set gain using the 20 nM standard well.

substeps.instruction: Subtract the blank (0 nM) fluorescence from all measurements.

steps.title: Generate calibration curve and calculate concentration
steps.instruction: Plot blank‑subtracted fluorescence versus known GFP concentrations; fit a linear trend line (y = mx + b); compute sample concentrations using the equation and correct for the 1:10 dilution; verify R² > 0.95, otherwise adjust the standard range.

steps.title: Prepare passivated flow‑cell slide
steps.instruction: Clean microscope slides and passivate with mPEG‑Silane containing ~2 % biotin‑PEG‑Silane as described; store slides frozen until use.

steps.title: Assemble flow‑cell chamber
steps.instruction: Warm slides to room temperature (~20 min); apply double‑sided tape in two long‑edge stripes covering ~1/3 of the PEG surface, leaving a central canal; add vacuum grease in two lines just above the drilled holes using a 1 mL syringe with a 200 µL tip; place a cleaned passivated coverslip on top, align over the grease, and gently rub the taped area with a blunt scalpel to seal; cut off excess tape.

steps.title: Immobilize NeutrAvidin on slide
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL T50 buffer to the flow cell, check for leaks and wipe outflow with a Kimwipe; add 70 µL 0.2 mg/mL NeutrAvidin; incubate 10 min at room temperature protected from light; wash twice with 70 µL T50 buffer, wiping each outflow.

steps.title: Add biotinylated antibody
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL biotinylated antibody (20 nM in T50) specific for the target protein; incubate 20 min at room temperature protected from light; wash twice with 70 µL T50 buffer.

steps.title: Introduce DIBMALPs sample
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL DIBMALP preparation diluted to 100 pM–10 nM in T50 buffer; incubate 30 min at room temperature protected from light.

steps.title: Wash and add oxygen scavenger
steps.instruction: Wash the flow cell three times with 70 µL T50 buffer (Kimwipe each outflow); add 70 µL fresh OSS solution, keep protected from light.

steps.title: Acquire single‑molecule TIRF videos
steps.instruction: Mount the slide on the TIRF microscope stage, attach the prism, and excite with the appropriate laser (e.g., 465 nm); record 10–12 videos per condition with 100 ms exposure for 500–1 000 frames using the provided IDL analysis script.
